note_en: Situations the review panel will put to every scheme. Not a checklist to fill in: a scheme that has worked out its city will already have an answer to most of them.

scenarios.title: A 44 degree afternoon
scenarios.prompt: It is the hottest hour of the year. Where can a person walk, stand and wait outdoors, and what is keeping them alive?
must_answer_en: Where on the plan is the main shaded walking network, and what share of it is shaded?
What part does water play in that shade, and is it in the water balance?
scenarios.why_en: Whether walking works at all in this desert depends on this one.

scenarios.title: Grid export hour
scenarios.prompt: Solar is at peak and compute demand is below generation. What does the district do with the surplus?
must_answer_en: Where does the surplus go: export, storage, or conversion into compute or hydrogen?
What does that choice assume about connection capacity (not supplied by the organiser - declare it)?
scenarios.why_en: How surplus is handled sizes the substations and transmission corridors, and so the city's skeleton.

scenarios.title: Grid import hour
scenarios.prompt: It is 21:00, generation is near zero, compute load is flat. Where does the power come from and what does that cost the carbon claim?
must_answer_en: Where does power come from in these hours: storage, grid import, or load reduction?
What is the hourly carbon-free match as a result - physical self-supply or contractual matching?
If cut off from the provincial grid for 72 hours, can the city run islanded, for how long, and which loads come first?
scenarios.why_en: Daytime solar is easy. This brief is about the night.

scenarios.title: Water is 30% short
scenarios.prompt: The assumed allocation does not arrive. What is curtailed first, and who decides?
must_answer_en: Which use stops first: compute cooling, agriculture, landscape, domestic? Give the order.
What happens in the city after each step - what stops, how many people are affected?
Does compute load come down with it, and can the contracts allow that?
scenarios.why_en: This separates serious schemes from renderings. A scheme that avoids it scores nothing on D2 here.

scenarios.title: A delivery robot and a child
scenarios.prompt: They meet on the same surface. What has been designed so that this is unremarkable?
must_answer_en: Separated, mixed or time-shared - which applies here, and how is it enforced?
How many such at-grade human-machine interfaces are there in the scheme?
scenarios.why_en: No current code answers this. The scheme has to take a position.

scenarios.title: Night shift ends
scenarios.prompt: A worker leaves a facility at 03:00. What is open, lit, and safe between there and home?
must_answer_en: At 3 a.m., what is open, lit and safe between the facility and home?
How do night lighting and light-pollution control both hold?
scenarios.why_en: A city that works only by day is not a city; it is a campus.

scenarios.title: Dust event
scenarios.prompt: A wind event puts dust in the air for two days. What happens to cooling, to solar yield, and to public space?
must_answer_en: Can outdoor public space still be used during the event, and where do people go?
Are soiling losses and cleaning water in the water balance?
How are air-cooled intakes protected from dust, and what is the stance of street sections and orientation to the wind - block, channel or step aside?
scenarios.why_en: The Zonda hits generation, water and outdoor life at once. Answered separately, something is missed.

scenarios.title: The anchor tenant leaves
scenarios.prompt: The compute operator exits in year eight. What of phase one survives, and what was designed to be convertible?
must_answer_en: Who owns the compute asset, who takes it over, and what do the contracts say?
How does the population that depends on compute jobs make the transition?
Which phase-one buildings were designed to be converted?
scenarios.why_en: A city whose economy rests on one asset must answer this; not answering leaves the risk with the residents.

scenarios.title: A resident asks a question
scenarios.prompt: Someone wants to know how much water the district used last month. What do they do, and what do they get?
must_answer_en: She wants to know how much water the city used last month. Where does she ask, and what does she get?
Who publishes it, how often, and who can check it independently?
scenarios.why_en: Public auditability is not a promise; it is a mechanism with an address, a frequency and someone responsible.

scenarios.title: First 500 people
scenarios.prompt: Phase one opens. Who are the first 500 people here all day, and what is their day like?
must_answer_en: Who are these 500 people, what do they do, and what is their day like?
Do day-one jobs and residents reconcile?
scenarios.why_en: A city that does not work on day one will not work on day ten thousand.

scenarios.title: Construction year three
scenarios.prompt: Half the parcel is a building site. What does the finished half feel like to be in?
must_answer_en: With half the site under construction, what is it like to be in the finished half?
How does construction traffic relate to the occupied areas?
scenarios.why_en: Phasing is not three drawings; every year of it has to be liveable.

scenarios.title: Phase two is triggered
scenarios.prompt: The conditions are met. What in phase one has to change, and what was left open to allow it?
must_answer_en: What is the trigger - population, occupancy, grid, water? It must be observable.
Which phase-one decisions can no longer be changed at this point, and why is that acceptable?
scenarios.why_en: Phase one is the first piece of a city, not a standalone project; the irreversible decisions show here.

scenarios.title: Flash flood in a dry wash
scenarios.prompt: An upstream storm puts flood flow down the dry washes on the alluvial fan within tens of minutes. What is in its path?
must_answer_en: Where are the flood corridors on the plan, and what is the basis for their width?
Which roads, pipes and substations cross a flood corridor, and how?
Confirm that no permanent construction sits on a dry channel.
scenarios.why_en: This is the one outside schemes miss most often. A scheme that treats a dry channel as flat ground scores low on D1.

scenarios.title: The day after a design-level earthquake
scenarios.prompt: A design-level earthquake. Structures stand, but power, water and communications are down. What happens next?
must_answer_en: Where do people go: the location and capacity of refuge space on the plan.
How does compute fail: shutdown, reduced load, or islanded operation?
Which lifeline is restored first, and on what basis?
scenarios.why_en: Structures standing is not the same as the city working.
